newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-AUSTRALIAN STUART APPLEBY WINS FIRST PGA TITLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-AUSTRALIAN STUART APPLEBY WINS FIRST PGA TITLE.

text.p: Australian Stuart Appleby won his first PGA Tour event Sunday, shooting a one-under-par 71 in the final round to win the $1.5 million Honda Classic by a stroke.
Appleby's 14-under-par total of 274 edged out Payne Stewart, who also shot 71, and Michael Bradley, who had a 68. Britain's Colin Montgomerie was in fourth place at 11 under par after his 71.

"To win my second year on tour is awesome. I'm very satisfied," said Appleby. The 25-year-old, who grew up on a dairy farm in the small town of Cohuna, Australia, won twice on the Nike tour in 1995, failed to keep his PGA Tour card last year, but made it through qualifying school this year.

Appleby held the lead after three rounds by a stroke, but had little time to worry or get nervous. The time lapse between the last two rounds, thanks to Friday's washout, was 12 minutes as the third and final rounds were both played Sunday.
He lost the lead to Stewart after bogeys on the first two holes, and did not regain the lead until the 14th hole, when Appleby holed a 65-yard wedge shot from the deep rough for eagle.

"That was one of those shots you just hope you can get it within 10 feet. I saw that the bounce was friendly, and I knew by the crowd that it was going to be within 10 feet, then bang, it went in. When you win, there's usually one hole, or one bounce that makes the difference," said Appleby.

For Stewart the difference wasn't Appleby's eagle "though it's too bad we can't play defence in this game -- I could've guarded that shot," said Stewart. "The golf tournament was mine to win and I didn't do it."
There were several putts that could have helped Stewart win, and on the 12th hole he let his lead drop from two strokes to one when he missed a two-foot putt for par.
Playing behind Appleby and Stewart, Bradley had a chance to force a play-off, but a 25-foot putt for birdie on the last hole finished a few inches outside of the hole.
"It was a long day. My iron play wasn't very good at all. I just didn't get the ball close enough when I needed to, but my putter kept me in it," said Bradley.
For Appleby the win was worth $270,000, and put him into 10th place on the 1997 money list with $304,431. It also got him an exemption into the Masters next month.

"The only Masters I've ever played in is the Australian Masters. I never even grew up thinking about playing in the Masters, that felt so far away. I'm going to be nervous just getting to the driveway," said Appleby.
